title: Secrets Versus Configuration Variables knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Secrets Versus Configuration Variables?
options: Use secrets for credentials and `vars` for non-sensitive configuration; place each at the narrowest repository/environment/organization scope that fits.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: Use secrets for credentials and `vars` for non-sensitive configuration; place each at the narrowest repository/environment/organization scope that fits.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of secrets versus configuration variables: Use secrets for credentials and `vars` for non-sensitive configuration; place each at the narrowest repository/environment/organization scope that fits.
